title: The Irish Channel dances
summary: With Ernest Johnson he played Irish Channel dances; trouble was stopped by music.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Did you play in Irish Channel?

Yeah, I played Irish Channel every time. See, when I was playing music with Ernest Johnson, Doug Ernest, he lived down in Irish Channel, around St. Thomas Street. And he used to get white... He knew these people out there, see. And he used to get white from these people, whatever dances they had. They were pretty quiet bunch of people?
Yeah, they were nice people. I didn't find nothing wrong with them. No?
Did they give you a nice... Oh yeah, yeah, yeah.

The only thing we had to do was what I'm saying every now and then, a couple of these youngsters would start a little fight, and they'd say, play music, bands play music, they're fighting. All I had to do was play any little thing, you know. Couple of boys or anything, and then stop the fight. No fight, no trouble, we never had no trouble.
